last_digest.title: Large group of Serbian opposition, activist figures targeted with spyware
last_digest.rss_summary: At least 14 Serbians have been targeted with advanced spyware since December, with victims including a member of Parliament, a local opposition politician and student protesters, according to digital forensic researchers.

last_week_digest.title: FBI takes down China-linked hacking network behind attacks on NASA, DOJ and U.S. Senate
last_week_digest.tldr: The FBI dismantled a Chinese-linked hacking network, QTFY, which compromised critical infrastructure including NASA and the Department of Justice. By seizing domains, authorities disabled malware used for global espionage, signalling an aggressive international shift toward proactively disrupting state-sponsored cyber operations targeting essential government services.

last_week_digest.title: ATF confirms “major incident” after recent Qilin breach claims
last_week_digest.tldr: The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives confirmed a major security incident following claims by the Qilin ransomware gang. While operations remain unaffected, this breach highlights the persistent vulnerability of government agencies to sophisticated criminal groups targeting critical infrastructure and sensitive data globally.

last_week_digest.title: AnonyMousKIT phishing-as-a-service uses AI voice calls to steal iPhone passcodes
last_week_digest.tldr: The AnonyMousKIT phishing-as-a-service platform uses AI voice agents to steal Apple ID credentials, enabling thieves to unlock stolen iPhones. Operating across 506 domains, this criminal enterprise demonstrates how automated social engineering now monetises stolen hardware, signalling a sophisticated, scalable shift in global mobile cybercrime.

last_week_digest.title: Exclusive: NSA to host a hacker reunion in bid to rebuild secretive unit
last_week_digest.tldr: The US National Security Agency is hosting an exclusive reunion for hundreds of former Tailored Access Operations hackers to bolster recruitment. This unconventional strategy highlights the intense global competition for elite cyber talent, signalling that intelligence agencies are increasingly prioritising aggressive human capital retention strategies.

last_week_digest.title: US Disrupts Chinese Hacking Platform Used in Military and Critical Infrastructure Attacks
last_week_digest.tldr: International authorities have dismantled the QTFY hacking platform, a service provider facilitating state-sponsored cyberattacks against global military and critical infrastructure. This disruption highlights the growing operational risk posed by commercialised cyber-espionage tools, signalling a shift towards targeting the infrastructure supporting sophisticated, persistent threat actors.

last_week_digest.title: Two Alleged ‘TeamPCP’ Hackers Arrested in Australia
last_week_digest.tldr: Australian authorities arrested two men linked to TeamPCP, a syndicate responsible for compromising over 3,800 GitHub repositories and harvesting cloud credentials from 2,500 global organisations via malicious open-source tools. This operation signals a shift toward incentivised, large-scale supply chain attacks, highlighting the critical vulnerability of global software ecosystems to sophisticated, distributed developer-focused exploitation strategies.

last_week_digest.title: Carhartt data breach exposes information of 12.9 million accounts
last_week_digest.tldr: The ShinyHunters extortion group leaked 50GB of data from clothing retailer Carhartt, compromising 12.9 million accounts after the company refused a $3.3 million ransom. This breach, stemming from a compromised analytics platform, highlights the severe operational risks posed by cloud-based data storage vulnerabilities and signals a growing trend of targeted extortion against major global enterprises.

last_week_digest.title: Dark Caracal Deploys New Go Malware With Ethereum-Based C2 Fallback
last_week_digest.tldr: The APT group Dark Caracal recently compromised a Venezuelan communications firm using the new GoCaracal malware and updated Bandook backdoors. By integrating Ethereum smart-contract fallbacks for command-and-control, the group ensures resilient, persistent access. This evolution signals a sophisticated trend where state-aligned actors leverage decentralised blockchain infrastructure to bypass traditional network security and maintain long-term espionage.

last_week_digest.title: Pro-Russian Hackers Claim Responsibility for Major Cyberattack on Norway’s Public Digital Services
last_week_digest.tldr: Pro-Russian group Server Killers has claimed responsibility for a significant cyberattack targeting Norway’s public digital infrastructure. This disruption hindered essential government services, highlighting the severe operational risks posed by state-aligned hacktivists. The incident signals a growing trend of politically motivated digital sabotage, forcing organisations globally to bolster resilience against increasingly frequent, disruptive attacks on infrastructure.

last_week_digest.title: Chinese and Russian spies stepping up cyberattacks, German companies report
last_week_digest.tldr: German businesses now attribute 40% of cyberattacks to foreign intelligence services, a sharp rise from 7% in 2023. These state-backed operations, primarily from China and Russia, cost the economy up to $240 billion annually. This shift signals a dangerous convergence between criminal syndicates and state actors, threatening global supply chains and critical industrial stability.

last_week_digest.title: In Other News: Log4j RCE Scare, Minimus Shutdown, Iranian Hacker Sanctions
last_week_digest.tldr: Manchester Airports Group recently suffered a significant cyberattack, highlighting persistent vulnerabilities in critical infrastructure. While Carhartt confirmed its data breach was partially fabricated, these incidents underscore the growing operational risks facing global enterprises. Such events signal that organisations must urgently refine their incident response strategies to mitigate the escalating financial and reputational damage from sophisticated threats.

last_week_digest.title: ATF confirms cyberattack hit system containing info on its investigation targets
last_week_digest.tldr: The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives confirmed a cyberattack on a standalone system containing sensitive investigation target data. While the agency maintains operations remain unaffected, the breach attributed to the Qilin ransomware group signals an alarming escalation in targeting federal law enforcement, highlighting the persistent, global threat posed by highly active, financially-motivated extortion syndicates.

last_week_digest.title: McKesson discloses breach after ShinyHunters claims patient data theft
last_week_digest.tldr: Healthcare giant McKesson recently suffered a significant data breach after the ShinyHunters group allegedly exfiltrated 284 million patient records via social engineering. This incident, impacting third-party applications, caused intermittent service degradation for global partners. It highlights the escalating risk of identity-based attacks against cloud environments, signalling that even robust enterprise systems remain vulnerable.

last_week_digest.title: Security Affairs newsletter Round 592 by Pierluigi Paganini – INTERNATIONAL EDITION
last_week_digest.tldr: Recent cyber incidents highlight escalating threats to global critical infrastructure and data privacy, notably the Manchester Airports Group breach impacting 8.7 million customers and the Love Electric theft of 877,000 driver records. These events signal a shift towards high-impact targeting of essential services, forcing organisations to prioritise robust supply chain security and proactive vulnerability management.

last_week_digest.title: PaperCut warns of hackers using printer management software flaw in attacks
last_week_digest.tldr: PaperCut has issued emergency patches for critical vulnerabilities in its print management software, which are currently under active exploitation by cybercriminals. These flaws allow attackers to gain initial network access, threatening global corporations and government entities. This incident signals that widely used, internet-facing administrative tools remain prime targets for ransomware gangs and state-backed actors.

last_week_digest.title: Attackers plant remote access tools on compromised PaperCut servers
last_week_digest.tldr: Threat actors are exploiting two zero-day vulnerabilities in PaperCut print management servers to install remote access tools, risking unauthorised network control. With 47% of tracked installations remaining unpatched, this incident highlights the critical operational danger of legacy software and the necessity for rapid patching.

last_week_digest.title: Healthcare Giant McKesson Investigates Data Breach Incident
last_week_digest.tldr: Healthcare giant McKesson is investigating a breach by ShinyHunters, potentially exposing 284 million records and triggering a $55 million ransom demand. This incident highlights critical supply-chain vulnerabilities, signalling that global organisations must urgently strengthen third-party application security to mitigate escalating risks from sophisticated extortion groups.

last_week_digest.title: NIS2 compliance: Fixing IAM and access control before the 2026 audit
last_week_digest.tldr: The EU’s NIS2 Directive now mandates strict access controls, threatening non-compliant firms with fines up to €10 million or 2% of global turnover. With credential abuse featuring in 39% of breaches, organisations must urgently secure service accounts to avoid audit failures and executive liability.

last_week_digest.title: Berlin says it won’t pay ransom after hackers steal government data
last_week_digest.tldr: Berlin officials have refused a $2.3 million ransom demand after the Rhysida group allegedly stole 5.79 terabytes of government data. The breach disrupted critical public services and ministries, signalling that public-sector entities remain high-value targets for global ransomware syndicates seeking sensitive information.

last_week_digest.title: Anthropic Warns Claude Users of Infostealer Malware Infections
last_week_digest.tldr: Anthropic is forcing global Claude users to reset accounts and remove payment details after infostealer malware compromised customer credentials. This preemptive measure highlights the growing risk of AI platforms becoming primary targets, signalling an urgent need for enhanced endpoint security across the enterprise sector.

last_week_digest.title: Stronger Security Drives Ransomware Groups to Recruit From Within
last_week_digest.tldr: Ransomware groups are increasingly recruiting malicious insiders, causing annual costs to reach $19.5 million per organisation. With malicious insider incidents rising by 42% and over 75% of dark web recruitment posts involving internal access, firms must recognise that hardened perimeters cannot mitigate the significant financial risks posed by compromised staff.

last_week_digest.title: SonicWall warns of actively exploited SMA1000 zero-day flaws
last_week_digest.tldr: SonicWall has warned that threat actors are actively exploiting two zero-day vulnerabilities in SMA1000 remote access appliances, potentially compromising enterprise networks. With over 400 devices exposed globally, this incident highlights the persistent risk to critical infrastructure and signals an urgent industry need for rapid patching and robust identity security protocols.

last_week_digest.title: Attackers Access Aesto Health AWS Infrastructure, Exposing 9.5 Million Records
last_week_digest.tldr: Aesto Health suffered a significant security breach after attackers accessed its AWS infrastructure, exposing the personal and medical records of 9.5 million individuals. This incident highlights the critical vulnerability of healthcare technology providers, signalling that cloud-based data repositories remain prime targets for cybercriminals seeking to exploit sensitive patient information globally.

last_week_digest.title: Ransomware Gang Claims Nutex Health Data Breach
last_week_digest.tldr: Nutex Health recently confirmed a significant data breach after a ransomware gang accessed sensitive patient, employee, and financial records. This incident disrupts critical business operations and exposes the healthcare sector to heightened regulatory scrutiny, signalling that cybercriminals are increasingly targeting vulnerable medical databases to leverage high-value information for global extortion.

last_week_digest.title: China's 'Fire Ant' campaign used compromised Cisco routers as platform for more attacks
last_week_digest.tldr: The Fire Ant campaign, linked to group UNC3886, systematically compromised Cisco routers to infiltrate high-value networks between 2022 and 2026. By seizing control of critical infrastructure, attackers harvested credentials and monitored administrative traffic. This evolution signals a strategic shift, as adversaries now target foundational trust layers to facilitate persistent cross-network espionage.

last_week_digest.title: New pro-Ukraine hacker group targets Russian companies with custom ransomware
last_week_digest.tldr: Pro-Ukrainian group VantaCore is targeting Russian organisations with custom ransomware, impacting at least seven victims with multimillion-dollar demands. This shift towards proprietary malware signals a broader trend of hacktivist groups professionalising operations, moving away from shared tools to increase their long-term operational autonomy.

last_week_digest.title: Exploitation of Sangoma Switchvox flaw is underway (CVE-2026-9586)
last_week_digest.tldr: Threat actors are actively exploiting a critical SQL injection vulnerability in Sangoma Switchvox, jeopardising approximately 4,000 internet-exposed VoIP systems. This breach risks internal network compromise and malware deployment, signalling that rapid exploitation of discovered flaws is becoming the new norm for global digital infrastructure.

last_week_digest.title: US charges Russian for infecting 80,000 freelancers with malware
last_week_digest.tldr: A Russian national faces charges for infecting 80,000 freelancers with malware via phishing, enabling remote system control and credential theft. This incident highlights how attackers exploit trusted communication platforms to compromise global workforces, signalling an urgent need for robust endpoint security and identity verification.

last_week_digest.title: Iran-linked APT Mirage Kitten Uses Fake Job Tests to Spread Malware
last_week_digest.tldr: The Iran-linked APT Mirage Kitten is targeting software engineers via fake LinkedIn job assessments. By prohibiting AI tools, attackers successfully deploy NodeRabbit and PollCat malware, compromising systems globally. This trend signals a sophisticated shift toward exploiting recruitment processes to bypass automated security detection protocols.

last_week_digest.title: UK Moves to Block High-Risk Tech Suppliers From Critical Infrastructure
last_week_digest.tldr: The UK’s Cyber Security and Resilience Bill introduces ministerial powers to restrict high-risk technology suppliers from critical infrastructure. This legislative shift addresses escalating supply chain threats, signalling a global trend where governments prioritise national security over vendor convenience to protect essential services from systemic disruption.

last_week_digest.title: 2,000 Leaked Documents Reveal How Russia Turns Engineering Students Into GRU Cyber Operators
last_week_digest.tldr: Leaked documents from Bauman Moscow State Technical University reveal a covert pipeline training 250 students for Russian military intelligence operations. This clandestine department, linked to APT28 and Sandworm, signals a shift toward institutionalised state-sponsored cyber warfare. Such integration of academic curricula with offensive espionage capabilities highlights growing risks to global supply chain security.

last_week_digest.title: Thomson Reuters reveals breach that exposed U.S. and Canadian court records
last_week_digest.tldr: Thomson Reuters confirmed a breach of its C-Track platform, exposing sensitive personal data across court systems in twelve US states, the US Virgin Islands, and Canada. Unauthorized access occurring in March 2026 compromised records including Social Security numbers and medical information. This incident highlights the systemic risks inherent in third-party legal management software providers.

last_week_digest.title: Manchester Airports Group Data on 8.8 Million People Leaked After Ransom Refusal
last_week_digest.tldr: Manchester Airports Group suffered a significant data breach after refusing ransom demands, resulting in 550GB of sensitive information concerning 8.8 million people being leaked online. Exploiting exposed administrative keys, attackers demonstrated the severe operational risks posed by inadequate credential management, signalling a growing industry trend where threat actors weaponise stolen data following failed extortion attempts.

last_week_digest.title: Pegasus and NoviSpy Used Against Serbian Protesters
last_week_digest.tldr: Serbian activists and opposition figures face a major surveillance campaign, with at least 14 individuals targeted by Pegasus and NoviSpy spyware since early 2026. This zero-click exploitation of mobile devices signals a concerning global trend where state-sponsored actors leverage mercenary tools to suppress political dissent, undermining digital privacy and democratic integrity during critical elections.

last_week_digest.title: Large group of Serbian opposition, activist figures targeted with spyware
last_week_digest.tldr: At least 14 Serbian activists and opposition figures were targeted with Pegasus and NoviSpy spyware since December, facilitating systemic surveillance and public smear campaigns. This breach of privacy, occurring around critical elections, signals a concerning global trend where state actors increasingly weaponise sophisticated mobile exploits to suppress civil society and silence political dissenters worldwide.
